B: Hiya mate, how you doing? Craig. Can you hear me alright?
A: Hiya, yeah, loud and clear! Daniel. I'm in Newark, East Midlands.
B: Nice one. I'm Cottingham, just outside Hull. Last one of the day, this, isn't it? How you finding it?
A: Yeah, it's been good, actually. Everyone's been really nice. Bit nervous at the start, if I'm honest.
B: Nah, you're alright. I saw the Forest scarf on your shelf, by the way. I've been dying to say something.
A: Ha! Go on, then. I share a season ticket with my dad, we take turns on home games. I get far too wound up, though. Go dead quiet when we're losing.
B: I'm the opposite, mate, I never shut up. Hull FC, season ticket, me and the brother-in-law. Rugby league, though, so you can't have a go at me about football.
A: No, fair. I play five-a-side, though, Wednesday nights, lads from school.
B: Wednesdays! Same, when shifts let me. I'm on a chemical plant, Saltend, twelve-hour days and nights, so some weeks I'm there and some weeks I'm stood in a control room thinking about it. What do you do?
A: I'm a director at a lettings firm. Family business, my dad started it. About a hundred and forty properties round Newark. Tenants, landlords, contractors, that sort of thing.
B: Director, very posh. Do you get the calls at stupid o'clock?
A: All the time. Had one on a Sunday about a boiler, right in the middle of dinner. I'm terrible, I always answer. I hate letting people down.
B: See, that's good, though. People remember that. Here, did you talk to Tomasz, the sparky?
A: I did, yeah! He said Nicola told him I could give him work, which was nice of her.
B: He told me off, mate. I asked if I could run an extension lead out to my summerhouse, and he went, no. Just like that. Armoured cable, consumer unit, the lot. I've been nearly finishing that summerhouse for two years and now it's another job on top.
A: Ha! He's very thorough. I'd have him on our books tomorrow, honestly. Is it a big summerhouse?
B: Big enough for a fridge and a telly, that's the dream. Barbecue season, have the whole street round. Do you do much in the summer?
A: Family week in Cornwall most years. And Tenerife with the lads, I've done the same resort three times. Las Americas.
B: No way! Playa de las Americas, we did that. Big group. You was probably stood next to me at the bar, mate.
A: Ha, probably! It were a good laugh. I'm a nightmare with flights, though. I check in the second it opens.
B: I'm not even packed till the taxi's outside. Rachel, my wife, she does all that. Have you got a missus?
A: Girlfriend, Hannah. Eighteen months. She's a primary school teacher in Grantham.
B: Eighteen months, eh? Ring's coming, then, is it?
A: Er, ha, maybe. I think she'd like that, actually. It's, er, a big thing, isn't it. The money and everything.
B: It is, mate. But honestly, nobody's ever got it all sorted first. You just sort of crack on and it works out. Me and Rachel were skint when we bought ours. Best thing we did.
A: Yeah. No, that's good to hear, actually. I still live with my mum and dad, so, er, one step at a time.
B: Nothing wrong with that. You'll get there. Just don't let anyone talk you into a summerhouse, that's my only
A: Ha, noted! I'll tell Hannah you said
